reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence (CIN6) publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 143,000 square feet, the largest published data center campus in Kentucky by capacity.

This is more than half of Kentucky's published data center IT capacity, which totals 9.55 MW across three facilities with disclosed figures. Five facilities are mapped in the state, but most do not publish power specifications, so the actual installed base is likely larger. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks, a scale typical of enterprise and cloud colocation rather than a purpose-built AI training campus.

The facility's certifications cover financial services, healthcare, federal systems, and information security, which positions it for regulated workloads but says nothing about AI-specific infrastructure. Whether this campus becomes relevant to AI depends on retrofits for higher-density GPU deployments, local grid capacity for increased power draws, and investment decisions by its operator or acquirers. None of those factors appear in the published specifications, and the suitability score of 50 out of 100 reflects the absence of any announced expansion.
